newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy employers want longer metalworkers contract.
newsitem.headline: Italy employers want longer metalworkers contract.

text.p: Employers group Confapi said on Tuesday the new engineering and metalworkers' contract must be extended to 30 months from the standard two years.

In a statement after a meeting with the sector unions FIM, FIOM and UILM, Confapi said an extended contract was needed "in order to lighten the contract's costs and to enable companies to plan their employees's related costs."
The Confapi organisation represents 12,000 companies accounting for more than 400,000 of the sector's 1.7 million employees.
Confapi represents small and medium-sized businesses and is one of three employers' groups in the sector, where the bitter pay dispute has been going on since last June.

Italian media have widely reported that the largest organisation, Federmeccanica, has also requested an extension of the contract. The dispute centres on the interpretation of a landmark 1993 wage deal, which scrapped automatic index linked wage rises.
FIOM leader Claudio Damiani said on Monday it would never agree to a 30-month contract because this was a misinterpretation of the deal.
